subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the unit vector in the direction of the vector a = 2i + 3j + k.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find a unit vector in a given direction.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the magnitude
steps.margin_note: First mark. Square each component, add, take the root. √14 does not simplify, and leaving it as a surd is the expected answer — not a decimal.
steps.memory_tip: Square each component, add, take the root. √14 does not simplify — leave it as a surd.

recall.must_convey: That the magnitude of a is found as √(4+9+1) = √14.
accept: find the magnitude, square root of four plus nine plus one which is root fourteen
the modulus of a is root fourteen
square the components add them and take the root
first find mod a which is root fourteen

steps.why: A unit vector has length 1, so the only thing needed is the length you must divide by. That is why the magnitude always comes first.
common_mistakes: Adding the components instead of their squares.
Turning √14 into a decimal, which loses exactness.

steps.label: Divide by the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The unit vector is the vector over its own length. Leave the surd in the denominator — rationalising is not expected here.
steps.memory_tip: The unit vector is the vector over its OWN length. Rationalising is not expected here.

recall.must_convey: That the unit vector is a divided by |a|, giving (2i+3j+k)/√14.
accept: divide the vector by its magnitude to get two i plus three j plus k over root fourteen
the unit vector is a over mod a
divide each component by root fourteen
vector ni magnitude tho divide cheste unit vector vasthundi
answer is two i plus three j plus k by root fourteen

steps.why: Dividing by the length scales the vector to length 1 without turning it, which is exactly what "unit vector in the same direction" means.
common_mistakes: Dividing only one component by the magnitude.
